# Fetching-enabled context default: one original and separate probes

This packet targets only CV0.33.0
`test_fetcher_lifecycle.py::test_context_provisions_and_owns_a_backend`.
`original_context_default_oracle.py` executes the unchanged complete original
through pytest, then separately observes real implicit AIOHTTP backend creation,
exact issued component identity and two explicit context closes. The probe also
creates two actual lazy sessions without making network requests and proves that
each closes and the second session is new. Components, cache objects, issued
budget identity and retained context owner remain stable across close/recreation.
This is fresh Python lifecycle evidence, not native execution or HTTP trust proof.

The required oracle is pyHanko0.38.1/CV0.33.0 with assertions enabled. Actual
interpreter/version/module/source bytes are recorded in the output. The unused
requests_mock pytest plugin is explicitly disabled because its import probes
IPv6 binding; no original fixture, parameter or provider is excluded. Network
connect/send/DNS/bind attempts are denied and recorded. The original and separate
probe both produce zero such events in the initial run.

Native-generated CMS/HTTP outputs, signed/replayed revocation evidence and fresh
same-byte trust comparisons are separate later receipts. No prior fixture replay
is relabelled fresh generation. Ordinary native builder defaults remain disabled;
this packet is only the explicitly fetching-enabled L2 constructor adaptation.
No source-reachability, policy-handler handoff, Supplied(empty) presence mapping,
OS roots, unrelated provider support or universal parity claim follows.

`same_bytes_context_oracle.py` accepts exact native-receipted output files and
raw native logs plus the source-bound Cargo receipt. It independently checks the
lossless gzip archive against runtime ELF raw SHA256/length, all case receipts and
raw HTTP request/response bytes. Every exported revocation `ee`/`ca` value is mapped
to the exact pinned enum, not a weaker legacy mode. The same native CMS/content,
roots/time/local and actually served candidate bytes are validated offline on two
CMS surfaces; custom unsent native capabilities are not replaced with defaults.
Malformed 200 response bodies remain exact inputs: Python context-construction
exceptions are recorded with phase/class, and do not count as entered CMS APIs or
status parity. Native status refusals and earlier Python parsing refusals may both
withhold trust while differing in error phase. Successful native OK versus Python
None subindication is also retained as a representation difference.

The first source7d2 cohort contains8 actual exported cases,16 context-build
attempts,14 actual CMS API calls and2 malformed-material constructor refusals.
All14 comparable flag/bottom-line results agree; no excluded case or network
attempt. This frozen cohort is not relabelled as execution of a later Git head.
Fresh signatures/native HTTP evidence remain separate from the explicitly
committed root-CRL and local-evidence replay. No function count changes here.
